text: Which one of the following predicate formulae is NOT logically valid? Note that W is a predicate formula without any free occurrence of x.
options: (for all x)(p(x) or W) is equivalent to (for all x p(x)) or W
(there exists x)(p(x) and W) is equivalent to (there exists x p(x)) and W
(for all x)(p(x) implies W) is equivalent to (for all x p(x)) implies W
(there exists x)(p(x) implies W) is equivalent to (for all x p(x)) implies W
solution: W has no free x, so the quantifier slides past it for and and or: (A) and (B) are valid. For (C), rewrite p implies W as not p or W. Then (for all x)(not p(x) or W) is (for all x not p(x)) or W, that is not (there exists x p(x)) or W - the existential, not the universal. Option (D) is the valid arrow case: (there exists x)(not p(x) or W) is (there exists x not p(x)) or W, which is (for all x p(x)) implies W.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page for GATE CS 2020 Q.39 with the accepted solution
answer_evidence: The accepted answer rewrites (C) as (there exists x P(x)) implies W and concludes (C) is not logically valid, while (D) is valid.
